assumptions: you accept a camera balance test is a demo and not an instrument
you have a clinician to define what an alert obliges anyone to do
clone_cost.estimate: 3 weeks for the test battery plus baseline detector
clone_cost.why: the tests are standard web tasks and the detector is a small scikit-learn job over a per-user series; no training is implied

hazard_note: Head-injury monitoring with alerting. The page disclaims diagnosis and refuses unsafe claims, which is the right posture, but an alert that a patient reads as clearance is a clinical event; anything built from this needs an explicit escalation path and a review by a clinician.

prior_art.relation: same name and problem, different team and a far more specified architecture (deterministic extraction, retrieval, escalation precedence); treat it as the stronger record of the two
concussion and ADHD recovery app that also triages symptoms; adds therapy automation the monitoring framing avoids
same bet - video plus computer vision to turn movement into interpretable evidence - in a different injury domain

what_breaks_first: The physical test. MediaPipe pose through a laptop webcam degrades with lighting, framing and a person who has vertigo, so the anomaly detector starts flagging the camera rather than the recovery; second, distribution - a monitoring tool with no clinical pathway has nowhere to send a bad reading.
what_to_steal: Baseline-relative anomaly detection as the product's whole claim: never assert a norm, assert deviation from the user's own series. It converts a small sample into a usable signal and it is honest about what it is.
worth_note: The framing is right - measure the person against their own baseline instead of a population threshold - and that transferable piece survives even though nothing about this build is checkable: no dataset, no metric, no repo, and a browser webcam asked to judge balance in someone who is dizzy.
